decision.when: When: The agent returns a correct summary but used an unauthorized tool.
decision.choice: Fail the test because action validity matters independently from answer quality.
decision.reason: Action traces expose unauthorized tool use that final-answer scoring cannot reveal.
decision.reject: Do not pass an agent because its final summary is correct. It may have used an unauthorized tool or argument.

workedTrace: Case: The agent returns a correct summary but used an unauthorized tool.
Check: Inspect tool choice, arguments, action order, permission result, and task completion.
Act: Fail the case on the unauthorized action. Check tool choice, arguments, order, permission, and side effects.
Test: Measure valid tool choice, authorized arguments, correct action order, and completion.

failure.symptom: The final response is correct, but the trace shows an unauthorized tool call.
failure.check: Inspect tool choice, arguments, action order, permission result, and task completion.
failure.fix: Fail the case on the unauthorized action. Check tool choice, arguments, order, permission, and side effects.

experiment.change: Change one tool schema or policy and compare action traces on the same scenarios.
experiment.observe: Measure valid tool choice, authorized arguments, correct action order, and completion.
experiment.limit: A successful simulated trace does not prove live integration reliability.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The final summary does not erase an unsafe action. Inspect the trace and fail when tool use exceeds the approved permission.

title: Evaluation reporting
principle: Report enough context for stakeholders to make a release decision. State sample, versions, criteria, and limits.
prerequisites: Know the stakeholder decision and its release criteria.
Record sample, dataset, rubric, model, and prompt versions.
mechanism: Compare baseline and candidate across quality, safety, latency, cost, and relevant segments. Show uncertainty and important failures.

decision.when: When: A score improves but the report omits sample composition and test version.
decision.choice: Require dataset, rubric, model, and prompt versions before making a decision.
decision.reason: Versions, sample composition, segments, and failures let reviewers interpret whether a score supports the release decision.
decision.reject: Do not report only a precise average. It can hide sample bias, segment failures, and uncertainty.

workedTrace: Case: A score improves but the report omits sample composition and test version.
Check: Inspect sample count, dataset version, rubric, segment results, and stated limits.
Act: Add dataset and configuration versions, sample context, segment results, and material failures to the report.
Test: Measure whether decision makers can interpret results with sample and segment context.

failure.symptom: The report shows a higher average but omits test version, sample makeup, or critical failures.
failure.check: Inspect sample count, dataset version, rubric, segment results, and stated limits.
failure.fix: Add dataset and configuration versions, sample context, segment results, and material failures to the report.

experiment.change: Add a segment breakdown and test whether the release recommendation changes.
experiment.observe: Measure whether decision makers can interpret results with sample and segment context.
experiment.limit: A chart cannot replace review of material failure examples.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The score lacks context for a release decision. Verify the sample, versions, segments, and failures before interpreting the change.

title: Deployment validation
principle: Validate a model or prompt update before expanding user exposure. Define stop conditions.
prerequisites: Set baseline output quality and stop conditions.
Prepare synthetic workflows and a rollback path before release.
mechanism: Run synthetic workflows and regression tests. Compare output, hallucination indicators, semantic drift, latency, and cost.

decision.when: When: A canary has acceptable latency but new unsupported claims.
decision.choice: Pause expansion and review quality evidence before rollout.
decision.reason: A quality regression is a stop signal even when canary latency remains acceptable. Rollback rules limit exposure.
decision.reject: Do not expand a canary because latency is healthy. That ignores unsupported claims and other quality failures.

workedTrace: Case: A canary has acceptable latency but new unsupported claims.
Check: Compare canary and baseline for safety, quality, drift, latency, and cost.
Act: Pause expansion. Compare quality and safety with the baseline, then use the tested rollback path if required.
Test: Measure canary quality, safety, drift, latency, and cost against a fixed baseline.

failure.symptom: The canary meets latency targets but produces unsupported claims absent from the baseline.
failure.check: Compare canary and baseline for safety, quality, drift, latency, and cost.
failure.fix: Pause expansion. Compare quality and safety with the baseline, then use the tested rollback path if required.

experiment.change: Add one recent failure workflow to the release suite and verify canary response.
experiment.observe: Measure canary quality, safety, drift, latency, and cost against a fixed baseline.
experiment.limit: Canary results apply to its tested traffic and observation period.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: Latency does not offset unsupported claims. Compare the canary output with the fixed baseline and stop expansion until quality passes.

title: Context handling diagnosis
principle: Find what content the model actually received. Count all prompt components and output reserve.
prerequisites: Know the complete request shape and model token limit.
Define the facts and output fields that must survive context reduction.
mechanism: Inspect request size, truncation behavior, stop reason, retrieved chunks, and validation errors. Reduce irrelevant history or evidence.

decision.when: When: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation.
decision.choice: Inspect token use and prompt assembly, then remove or summarize tested history.
decision.reason: The serialized request and stop evidence distinguish input truncation from output token exhaustion.
decision.reject: Do not raise the output token limit before checking input assembly. That cannot restore omitted input and may exceed the request budget.

workedTrace: Case: The model omits the final instruction after a long conversation.
Check: Inspect serialized request, token budget, truncation evidence, and stop reason.
Act: Inspect token use and truncation. Preserve required context with a tested summary before tuning output limits.
Test: Measure required content retained in the serialized request and completeness of the answer.

failure.symptom: The final instruction is absent from the serialized request before inference.
failure.check: Inspect serialized request, token budget, truncation evidence, and stop reason.
failure.fix: Inspect token use and truncation. Preserve required context with a tested summary before tuning output limits.

experiment.change: Change one context component and verify required facts remain in the actual request.
experiment.observe: Measure required content retained in the serialized request and completeness of the answer.
experiment.limit: Token estimation can vary by model tokenizer and request structure.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The request omitted the instruction before generation. Fix context assembly and verify its presence before changing output limits.

title: Inference integration diagnosis
principle: Classify API errors before changing model or prompt behavior. Preserve the exact request and caller context.
prerequisites: Capture the exact request, operation, model, role, and Region.
Know the API schema and error class for the selected call.
mechanism: Check operation, model identifier, Region, permissions, request schema, size limits, throttling, timeout, and response parsing. Inspect relevant service errors and request IDs.

decision.when: When: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change.
decision.choice: Compare the serialized request with the operation’s supported schema.
decision.reason: The exact operation schema identifies a malformed field, while the same-role replay tests the correction.
decision.reject: Do not retry an unchanged invalid request. Retries do not change the schema error or permission decision.

workedTrace: Case: A request fails with ValidationException after an API field change.
Check: Inspect operation, serialized fields, model identifier, role, Region, and error code.
Act: Compare serialized fields with the selected operation schema. Correct the invalid field before replay.
Test: Measure whether the corrected request succeeds under the same role, model, and Region.

failure.symptom: The same malformed request repeatedly returns ValidationException after the field change.
failure.check: Inspect operation, serialized fields, model identifier, role, Region, and error code.
failure.fix: Compare serialized fields with the selected operation schema. Correct the invalid field before replay.

experiment.change: Change one request field and replay the same call under the same role and Region.
experiment.observe: Measure whether the corrected request succeeds under the same role, model, and Region.
experiment.limit: Service errors can change. Use current service documentation and logs.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The repeated validation error identifies a request-shape problem. Check the operation and field types, then replay the corrected request once.

title: Prompt behavior diagnosis
principle: Treat prompt quality as a testable interaction among instructions, evidence, examples, and output contract.
prerequisites: Keep fixed cases and a versioned prompt baseline.
Know the required response contract and evaluation rubric.
mechanism: Use a fixed failure set and compare prompt versions. Check instruction conflicts, missing context, examples, variable substitution, and schema validation.

decision.when: When: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear.
decision.choice: Compare schema validity and task criteria across the old and new prompt versions.
decision.reason: A one-component prompt comparison isolates which instruction change caused required fields to disappear.
decision.reject: Do not rewrite several instructions at once. That prevents causal attribution and can add conflicts.

workedTrace: Case: A prompt update improves tone but causes required fields to disappear.
Check: Diff prompt versions and rendered variables, then inspect failures against the rubric.
Act: Diff the prompt and rendered variables. Change one component per test and score the fixed rubric.
Test: Measure rubric failures and schema validity after changing one prompt component.

failure.symptom: Required fields disappear after a prompt update that changed several instructions and examples together.
failure.check: Diff prompt versions and rendered variables, then inspect failures against the rubric.
failure.fix: Diff the prompt and rendered variables. Change one component per test and score the fixed rubric.

experiment.change: Change one instruction or example and measure exact failure categories on fixed cases.
experiment.observe: Measure rubric failures and schema validity after changing one prompt component.
experiment.limit: Prompt improvements may not transfer to unseen tasks.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The multi-change update obscures the cause. Compare rendered versions and isolate one changed component against the missing-field test.

title: Retrieval defect diagnosis
principle: Trace a missing or poor answer backward from generation to indexed source data.
prerequisites: Know source versions, sync state, chunking, and embedding settings.
Prepare labeled queries and expected retrieval results.
mechanism: Check source existence, latest sync, extraction quality, chunk boundaries, metadata filters, embedding compatibility, and ranking. Compare query and document vector configuration.

decision.when: When: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence.
decision.choice: Check ingestion state and filters, then inspect the indexed version and top results.
decision.reason: Source sync, index version, filters, and ranked results separate ingestion defects from query or generation defects.
decision.reject: Do not upgrade the model first. A model cannot retrieve a source absent from its evidence set or blocked by an access filter.

workedTrace: Case: A current policy exists in storage but never appears in retrieved evidence.
Check: Inspect source sync, chunk boundaries, embedding settings, filters, and ranked evidence.
Act: Check ingestion state, indexed version, filters, and rankings. Fix the first stage that drops the current source.
Test: Measure source freshness, relevant retrieval, and latency after the ingestion or query fix.

failure.symptom: The current source exists in storage, but sync or ranked retrieval evidence shows only an older version.
failure.check: Inspect source sync, chunk boundaries, embedding settings, filters, and ranked evidence.
failure.fix: Check ingestion state, indexed version, filters, and rankings. Fix the first stage that drops the current source.

experiment.change: Update one source record and trace it through ingestion and retrieval with a labeled query.
experiment.observe: Measure source freshness, relevant retrieval, and latency after the ingestion or query fix.
experiment.limit: A successful sync event does not prove useful retrieval.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: Storage presence does not prove index presence. Trace the source through sync and retrieval, then fix the first missing stage.

title: Prompt maintenance diagnosis
principle: Manage prompt templates as versioned application dependencies. Test variables, schema, and release links.
prerequisites: Know the prompt resource version and required variables.
Keep a known-good request trace and schema validation result.
mechanism: Inspect unresolved variables, incompatible request fields, prompt version, and changed instructions. Compare logs and traces with a known-good version.

decision.when: When: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text.
decision.choice: Inspect variable names and values at invocation, then test the rendered prompt.
decision.reason: Invocation-time bindings reveal why a valid stored template can render a literal placeholder at runtime.
decision.reject: Do not edit template wording before checking runtime bindings. The missing or stale value can persist after the edit.

workedTrace: Case: A deployed prompt version returns literal placeholder text.
Check: Inspect prompt version, variable bindings, request fields, schema result, and trace.
Act: Inspect deployed version and invocation variables. Correct bindings, then validate the rendered request.
Test: Measure rendered variable correctness and output validity for each prompt version.

failure.symptom: The deployed answer contains a literal placeholder although the stored template looks correct.
failure.check: Inspect prompt version, variable bindings, request fields, schema result, and trace.
failure.fix: Inspect deployed version and invocation variables. Correct bindings, then validate the rendered request.

experiment.change: Change one template variable contract and compare rendered requests and output validity.
experiment.observe: Measure rendered variable correctness and output validity for each prompt version.
experiment.limit: Logs can contain sensitive prompts and need strict access and retention.

masteryQuestion: Which evidence confirms this failure’s cause and supports the correction?
masteryAnswer: The literal placeholder shows that rendering failed. Compare the deployed version and bound variable names and values before editing prompt text.
